A linesheet is a sales document that fashion brands and wholesalers use to present their products to retail buyers for ordering. Unlike a lookbook, which focuses on styling and brand storytelling, a linesheet is built for purchasing decisions: it lays out each product alongside the practical details a buyer needs to place an order. A typical linesheet includes a clear product image, the style name and number, available colors and sizes, wholesale and suggested retail prices, minimum order quantities (MOQ), and delivery windows. Products are usually organized by category, season, or collection so buyers can scan quickly and reference exact specifications. Buyers review linesheets during market appointments or online to compare items, plan their assortments, and build orders. Because linesheets are transactional rather than promotional, they prioritize clarity, accuracy, and consistency over visual flourish. In digital wholesale platforms, linesheets are increasingly interactive—letting buyers filter, view product details, and order directly from the sheet. This streamlines the entire ordering process for both brands and retailers, reducing manual back-and-forth and errors.
